features.description: Singular-only common masculine/feminine and neuter hwā/hwæt NGDA; hwǣm primary, hwām valid variant. Distinct instrumental forms are reference only.
Question pronouns take the case their own function requires: subject nominative, possessor genitive, object accusative, recipient or governed dative.
Full strong hwilc/hwæðer/hūlic agreement in ordinary direct questions; hwæðer specifies two alternatives. No weak interrogative-adjective system assigned.

Direct yes/no questions commonly begin with the finite verb; wh-words or phrases commonly precede the finite verb, and a wh-subject is itself the subject. No English dummy do is added. These are tendencies, not an exceptionless V2 transformation.
Lexical hū how and hwȳ why in direct questions; hwȳ does not establish general instrumental syntax.
A finite verb commonly occurs early in an independent clause and later, often final, in a dependent/relative clause. Count constituents rather than words; avoid an obligatory order formula.
Ilca same is weak only; ordinarily article + ilca and weak agreement of any following adjective.

Self agrees with its referent; use strong/weak forms in ordinary emphasis, or add agreeing self to a personal reflexive accusative/dative. In Ic nęrie mē selfne the male speaker is both agent and object; selfne agrees with mē.

Ordinary attributive sum some/a certain, ǣnig any in questions, gehwilc each with singular noun, and swilc such; complete strong morphology. Following ordinary descriptive adjective in swilc phrases is strong. Extended negative/distributive/partitive/correlative constructions deferred.
Apply prior strong ōðer morphology to ordinary other/another, including after article; distinguish prior second sense.
Invariant ðe introduces an ordinary relative clause and can represent different internal case functions; it is not an English personal interrogative pronoun.
The inflected se/sēo/ðæt series can introduce relative clauses alone or followed by ðe; reuse its full NGDA morphology with newly taught relative function.

In selected productive relative clauses, gender and number track the antecedent while relative case is governed by its function within its own clause. An antecedent in dative can have a nominative relative, and vice versa; this is the selected ordinary construction, not a universal ban on attraction.

A relative subject with a personal-pronoun antecedent can carry that antecedent's person: ðū + ðe ... hulpe/gescēope takes second singular. Number/person must follow the intended antecedent, not the English word who.
Recognize that an inflected relative sometimes takes its antecedent's case rather than the case expected from its own internal function. No independent production of case attraction is assigned.
Recognize ðe plus a personal pronoun as an attested less common relative strategy; its inflected personal member marks the internal function. Full independent use deferred.
Recognize singular-only gehwā/gehwæt and its NGDA forms as an indefinite ge- compound. Independent indefinite/distributive syntax remains Unit15.
Productive ordinary countable lives with all plural līf/līfa/līfum/līf cells; retain prior formal-recognition history.

Libban may have the cognate accusative līf life, as in live our lives; the agreeing possessive is plural accusative. This is a bounded lexical construction, not permission to add objects to all intransitives.

Habban + accusative controlled entity + on + dative possessive/gewealde means have under one's control. On takes dative in this established control frame; spatial under is not mechanically substituted.
Promote gefyllan fill with an accusative thing/place filled. Earlier finish sense and source-only fill exposure do not establish independent fill production until this unit.
Complete present/preterite indicative and subjunctive of weakII ætēowian; selected i spellings retained.
Ætēowian is intransitive appear; the thing becoming visible is the nominative subject. Do not substitute transitive ætīewan display.
Complete scīnan present scīne/scīnen and preterite scine/scinen subjunctive systems, all persons; preserve two earlier supplied histories.
Both geblētsian commands: singular geblētsa, plural geblētsiað; direct-address target according to the prompt.
Cook I.8.13 supplies gesęte as a singular command; assign that exact support plus the local in-sea phrase. No full gesettan command or placement-government system follows from a parenthetic hint.

paradigms.title: hwā / hwæt NGDA
paradigms.scope: Singular only; one common masculine/feminine series and a neuter series. Productive ordinary subject, possessive, recipient/governed dative, direct-object accusative. No invented plural or separate feminine inflection.

paradigms.title: hwilc strong NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete strong NGDA, ordinary interrogative modifier or predicate. No weak paradigm or dependent-question construction assigned.

paradigms.title: hwilc distinct instrumental reference
paradigms.scope: Recognition of the distinct masculine/neuter singular forms only; all instrumental constructions remain outside Unit8.

paradigms.scope: Recognition of the distinct masculine/neuter singular forms only; all instrumental constructions remain outside Unit8.

paradigms.title: hwæðer strong NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete strong NGDA morphology; ordinary choice between two people, objects or explicitly plural groups. Plural morphology does not change the two-alternative meaning. Conjunction whether and indirect questions are unassigned.

paradigms.title: hwæðer distinct instrumental reference
paradigms.scope: Recognition of the distinct masculine/neuter singular forms only; all instrumental constructions remain outside Unit8.

paradigms.title: sum strong NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete strong NGDA morphology; ordinary attributive use. Extended partitives, negative concord, distributive correlations and free-choice clause syntax remain Unit15.

paradigms.title: sum distinct instrumental reference
paradigms.scope: Recognition of the distinct masculine/neuter singular forms only; all instrumental constructions remain outside Unit8.

paradigms.title: ǣnig strong NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete strong NGDA morphology; ordinary attributive use. Extended partitives, negative concord, distributive correlations and free-choice clause syntax remain Unit15.

paradigms.title: ǣnig distinct instrumental reference
paradigms.scope: Recognition of the distinct masculine/neuter singular forms only; all instrumental constructions remain outside Unit8.

paradigms.title: gehwilc strong NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete strong NGDA morphology; ordinary attributive use. Extended partitives, negative concord, distributive correlations and free-choice clause syntax remain Unit15. Selected ordinary each/every use with a singular noun; complete plural morphology is available for analysis, not a license to replace every contextual eall.

paradigms.title: gehwilc distinct instrumental reference
paradigms.scope: Recognition of the distinct masculine/neuter singular forms only; all instrumental constructions remain outside Unit8.

paradigms.title: swilc strong NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete strong NGDA morphology; ordinary attributive use. Extended partitives, negative concord, distributive correlations and free-choice clause syntax remain Unit15. Following ordinary attributive adjective remains strong in an indefinite phrase; distinct from already productive invariant swilce likewise.

paradigms.title: swilc distinct instrumental reference
paradigms.scope: Recognition of the distinct masculine/neuter singular forms only; all instrumental constructions remain outside Unit8.

paradigms.title: ilca weak NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete singular/plural NGDA; weak-only ilca or selected emphatic self according to its separate use rule. Weak instrumental is syncretic with dative, with no general instrumental syntax assigned.

paradigms.title: self strong NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete strong and weak NGDA. Agreement with the emphasized referent; nominative emphasis and accusative/dative reinforcement of a coreferential personal pronoun. Personal pronouns can be reflexive without self. No general modern English self-compounding rule.

paradigms.title: self distinct instrumental reference
paradigms.scope: Recognition of the distinct masculine/neuter singular forms only; all instrumental constructions remain outside Unit8.

paradigms.title: self weak NGDA
paradigms.scope: Complete singular/plural NGDA; weak-only ilca or selected emphatic self according to its separate use rule. Weak instrumental is syncretic with dative, with no general instrumental syntax assigned.

paradigms.title: ōðer strong NGDA, new other sense
paradigms.scope: New ordinary other/another sense; all24 existing strong NGDA forms retain their exact IDs/surfaces/ordinal analyses and prior teaching history. Forms remain strong even after article. No new ordinal milestone or indefinite reciprocal syntax.

paradigms.title: ōðer distinct instrumental reference
paradigms.scope: Earlier recognition scope only; no new general instrumental syntax.

paradigms.title: gehwā recognition reference
paradigms.scope: Recognition reference for the basic ge- compound of hwā: singular only, common masculine/feminine and neuter NGDA. Ordinary use, partitive combinations and independent production deferred to Unit15. No invented plural.

paradigms.title: se / sēo / ðæt relative NGDA
paradigms.scope: Ordinary inflected relative, alone or followed by ðe. Reuse all prior NGDA demonstrative cells; new relative sense/constructions only. Prefer case governed inside the relative in selected production; case attraction is a separately bounded recognition phenomenon.

paradigms.title: ætēowian finite indicative and subjunctive
paradigms.scope: WeakII intransitive appear. Complete present/preterite indicative and subjunctive only (24 logical cells). Infinitive and participle are citation recognition; commands and nonfinite syntax unassigned.

paradigms.title: scīnan full subjunctive
paradigms.scope: Add complete present/preterite subjunctive12 logical cells. Prior indicative/principal parts remain untouched; old supplied scīnen/scinen histories are deliberately promoted.

paradigms.title: geblētsian full command pair
paradigms.scope: Add both singular/plural commands; previous indicative/subjunctive teaching does not include these cells. Retain ge-; the source plain blētsode remains a different contextual exposure.

paradigms.title: līf full NGDA; plural promotion
paradigms.scope: Promote complete plural morphology for the ordinary countable lived-life sense; preserve all Unit1 recognition histories. Cognate accusative libban + līf taught separately.
